communications.subject: Florida Sunshine Law Request: Florida State Board of Immigration Enforcement Grant Narrative to Support September 2026 Cabinet Meeting Approval Request
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Florida Sunshine Law, I am writing to request the records to support the Grant Application Budget Details and Grant Award Budget Amendment Request Details (including each award ID#'s Budget Request Summary, Proposed Budget Details by Category, and Additional Justification narrative) for the following State Board of Immigration Enforcement Grant award requests (listed below by ID# and separated by a comma): 

IG128, IG134, IG136, IG137, IG138, IG139, IG141, IG002 AMD004, IG005 AMD002, IG008 AMD004, IG010 AMD004, IG013 AMD003, IG015 AMD005, IG016 AMD004, IG017 AMD003, IG018 AMD005, IG019 AMD003, IG022 AMD005, IG030 AMD005, IG031 AMD005, IG034 AMD004, IG036 AMD004, IG039 AMD004, IG040 AMD004, IG041 AMD006, IG042 AMD004, IG045 AMD004, IG049 AMD002, IG054 AMD003, IG055 AMD002, IG060 AMD002, IG073 AMD002, IG076 AMD004, IG077 AMD004, IG081 AMD005, IG083 AMD001, IG088 AMD004, IG091 AMD004, IG092 AMD004, IG094 AMD004, IG097 AMD002, IG103 AMD005, IG107 AMD000, IG114 AMD001, IG115 AMD001, IG116 AMD001, IG118 AMD001, IG143 VAN, IG144 VAN

If you withhold or redact any record, please identify and state the specific statutory basis for each withholding as required by statute and produce all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available (preferably a PDF or Excel spreadsheet if that's the native file-type) or on a CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Em D

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

An IHSC record showing the number, by month and year if possible, of Significant Event Notifications (SENs), Significant Incident Reports (SIRs), or similar records IHSC received for the period beginning May 6, 2025, and continuing through October 6, 2026, in which ICE ERO Field Office staff, ICE detention contractors, or IHSC Field Medical Coordinators who submitted the SEN or SIR checked the box next to "Death in Custody or Operations", "Hospital Admission," "Emergency Department Visit (ED", or "Serious Health Incidents Affected Bedspace Volume".

ICE previously fulfilled a request for these records from a prior timeframe under the FOIA request designated 2025-ICFO-36738. Please use the same methodology ICE FOIA used for that request to search for records responsive to this one. 

I seek expedited processing of this request pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e) and declare under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 U.S.C. 1746 that the following statements are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and understanding: 
1. I am a member of the media primarily engaged in information dissemination, and I have been granted expedited processing on this basis previously by federal FOIA agencies.  Examples of my edited works are available here: https://theappeal.org/authors/andrew-free/, here: https://atlpresscollective.com/author/free/, and here: https://assets.aclu.org/live/uploads/2024/06/2024-07-01-ICE-Detainee-Deaths.pdf. 
2. As ICE has rapidly increased its detained noncitizen population since January 2025, mortality in ICE custody has also rapidly increased. 
3. ICE is presently on track to allow more people to die in the agency's custody than in any year since FY2020, when the COVID19 pandemic ripped through facilities claiming lives until federal judges ordered targeted depopulation over ICE's objections. 

Table 1: Publicly Reported Deaths in ICE Custody by Fiscal Year since PBNDS 2011 adoption.
FY	COUNT of FY
11	10
12	8
13	9
14	6
15	7
16	10
17	12
18	10
19	9
20	22
21	5
22	3
23	4
24	12
25	10

4. Public reports indicate Congress intends to appropriate a roughly 900% increase in ICE detention funding, spending $45 billion to expand the deadly detention system. https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/07/us/politics/trump-administration-immigrant-detention-facilities-services.html. 
5. Timely access to information regarding healthcare outcomes in ICE custody is essential to public health researchers, medical experts, policymakers, and informed citizens who wish to have a meaningful role in the policy debate over whether the proposed budget increase represents a lawful and prudent expenditure of public resources. 
6. My previous FOIA work on ICE detention morbidity and mortality has resulted in obtaining records that have been shared with and cited by physicians, oversight agencies, Congress, and courts, influencing decisions that led to healthier outcomes for ICE's detained populations, and reducing the morbidity and mortality in ICE custody. 
7. There is an urgent need to inform the public regarding IHSC's capacity to manage and oversee medical emergencies and conditions that could lead to deaths of people in ICE custody. 

I respectfully request a fee waiver, as I will be publishing and circulating the results of the records I receive, and am not making this request for commercial purposes. 

Thank you in advance for your timely consideration of this time-sensitive request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Vincent M. Battle
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

- Personnel, assignment and performance records for Vincent Martin Battle (also known as Vincent M. Battle), a career Foreign Service officer who served from 1977 to approximately 2004, including assignment histories, Employee Evaluation Reports, promotion and tenure records, awards and commendations, and records of his retirement or separation, between January 1, 1977 and the date of search.
- Records relating to Mr. Battle's 2001 nomination and appointment as U.S. Ambassador to Lebanon, including biographical sketches, nomination and clearance packages, any questionnaire or statement prepared for the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, his confirmation hearing testimony, swearing-in records, and records of his presentation of credentials, between January 1, 2001 and December 31, 2001.
- Records relating to Mr. Battle's service as chargé d'affaires ad interim at U.S. Embassy Beirut in 1994 and as Ambassador to Lebanon from 2001 to 2004, including his arrival and farewell cables and any end-of-tour or end-of-mission reports, between January 1, 1994 and December 31, 2004.
- Records relating to Mr. Battle's volunteer, When Actually Employed (WAE) or other service at U.S. Embassy Beirut after his retirement, including during the July–August 2006 evacuation of U.S. citizens from Lebanon, between August 17, 2004 and the date of search, including the following words/phrases: "Battle," "Ambassador Battle," "Vince Battle," "volunteer," "WAE," "evacuation."

Please search, at a minimum, the Bureau of Global Talent Management (formerly the Bureau of Human Resources), the Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs, U.S. Embassy Beirut, the Bureau of Consular Affairs, the Office of the Historian and the Executive Secretariat, as well as the Department's central cable and records systems.

Mr. Battle is deceased. Proof of death is attached (U.S. Embassy Beirut statement of October 5, 2026, and published obituary). Because Mr. Battle has died, his privacy interest is greatly diminished, and records relating to his official public service as a senior U.S. diplomat carry substantial public interest.

I ask to be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Ramiro Valdés Menéndez (28 April 1932 – 21 June 2026)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of investigation or inquiry into U.S. diplomat Vincent Martin Battle (1940 – October 2026). His death is widely-known and widely reported; as such, privacy concerns under FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7 are voided, as are any concerns under the Privacy Act. For example, you may find his Le Orient Le Jour obituary at the following link: https://www.lorientlejour.com/article/1549739/hommage-a-vincent-battle-lambassadeur-pour-qui-le-liban-cetait-chez-lui.html

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records of both HQ and all field offices for all relevant names, agencies, organizations, companies and events including but not limited to those cited in the previous paragraphs and/or links as well as a cross-reference with the Southern Poverty Law Center to include any information provided by the SPLC. My request includes but is not limited to 137, 157, 176, 177, 183, 184, 188, and 214 files. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti
